The test `testNullCommentEqualsEmptyComment` in the class `ZipArchiveEntryTest` of the `org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.zip` package is intended to test whether a `ZipArchiveEntry` object with a null comment equals a `ZipArchiveEntry` object with an empty comment. The test creates three `ZipArchiveEntry` objects with the same name "foo" and sets their comments to null, empty, and "bar" respectively. It then asserts that the first two entries are equal.

1. Looking at the `ZipArchiveEntry.setComment` method, it simply assigns the provided comment to the `comment` field of the `ZipArchiveEntry` object.

2. The `ZipArchiveEntry.equals` method checks for equality between two `ZipArchiveEntry` objects by comparing their names, comments, and various attributes. In this case, it will compare the comments of the two entries.

Based on the test and the code snippets, the issue seems to be with how the `equals` method compares comments. Since one `ZipArchiveEntry` object has a null comment and the other has an empty comment, they are considered unequal because `myComment.equals(otherComment)` will fail when `myComment` is null.
This discrepancy causes the test to fail even though logically, a null comment and an empty comment should be considered equivalent.

Next, let's suggest the methods that need to be fixed to resolve this issue.
```java
org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.zip.ZipArchiveEntry.equals(java.lang.Object)
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
